title: Azgor or King Izgadar
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman describes a Persian king in Rav Ashi’s time who loved and honored the sages of Israel. In [Zevachim 19a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.19a.2), Rav Ashi says, “Huna bar Natan told me: Once I was standing before King Azgader, and he lifted my belt.” In [Ketubot 61a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.61a.16), Ameimar, Mar Zutra and Rav Ashi were at the entrance to King Azgor’s house.

Hyman cites the Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon, part 3, chapter 4, for another King Izgadar, whom he describes as wicked, in the time of Mar bar Rav Ashi. Hyman says he was the first king’s grandson and refers to S. Y. Rapoport’s discussion in Erekh Milin.[^1]

notes.text: The consulted Zevachim has Izgaddar, and Ketubot has Izgur. The relationship between the two kings is Hyman’s account. His exact Epistle and Erekh Milin references remain uncollated.
